claims.text: What the strip looks like Osborn (J) waves — a positive deflection at the J point — with bradycardia, prolonged intervals and muscle tremor artifact.
claims.quote: Osborn (J) waves — positive deflection at J point Bradycardia, prolonged intervals, muscle tremor artifact

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) J point: Osborn (J) wave — a positive deflection at the J point (negative in aVR and V1), usually most prominent in the precordial leads
claims.quote: The Osborn wave (J wave) is a positive deflection at the J point (negative in aVR and V1). It is usually most prominent in the precordial leads.

claims.text: The height of the Osborn wave is roughly proportional to the degree of hypothermia
claims.quote: The height of the Osborn wave is roughly proportional to the degree of hypothermia

claims.text: Rate and rhythm: bradycardia is common — sinus bradycardia (may be marked), AF with slow ventricular response, slow junctional rhythms, varying degrees of AV block (1st–3rd)
claims.quote: Bradycardia is a common finding in hypothermia. Patients may manifest a variety of bradyarrhythmias: Sinus bradycardia (may be marked) Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response Slow junctional rhythms Varying degrees of AV block (1st-3rd)

claims.text: Intervals: prolonged PR, QRS and QT
claims.quote: Prolonged PR, QRS and QT intervals

claims.text: Baseline: muscle tremor (shivering) artifact
claims.quote: Osborn (J) waves — positive deflection at J point Bradycardia, prolonged intervals, muscle tremor artifact

claims.text: Also: ventricular ectopics; cardiac arrest from VT, VF or asystole
claims.quote: Ventricular ectopics Cardiac arrest due to VT, VF or asystole

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Definition: core temperature < 35 °C — mild 32–35, moderate 29–32, severe < 29 °C
claims.quote: Hypothermia is defined as a core body temperature of < 35 °C [degrees centigrade]: Mild hypothermia is 32-35 °C Moderate hypothermia is 29-32 °C Severe hypothermia is < 29 °C

claims.text: Mechanism: hypothermia slows all physiologic functions, including the cardiovascular and respiratory systems, nerve conduction, mental acuity, neuromuscular reaction time, and metabolic rate
claims.quote: Hypothermia slows all physiologic functions, including cardiovascular and respiratory systems, nerve conduction, mental acuity, neuromuscular reaction time, and metabolic rate.

claims.text: Predisposing: conditions causing loss of consciousness and/or immobility (e.g., trauma, hypoglycemia, seizures, stroke, drug or alcohol intoxication); older adults and the very young are at high risk
claims.quote: Conditions that cause loss of consciousness, immobility, or both (eg, trauma, hypoglycemia, seizure disorders, stroke, drug or alcohol intoxication) are common predisposing factors (1, 2). Older adults and the very young also are at high risk

claims.text: Hypoadrenalism and hypothyroidism (including myxedema) can contribute and are often occult
claims.quote: Hypoadrenalism and hypothyroidism (including myxedema) can contribute to hypothermia and are often occult

claims.text: Symptoms Intense shivering first, then impaired movement; shivering then stops, so temperature falls faster
claims.quote: Intense shivering occurs initially, followed by impairment in movement. Shivering then progressively ceases, which allows body temperature to drop more precipitously.

claims.text: Lethargy and clumsiness, then confusion, irritability, sometimes hallucinations, and eventually coma
claims.quote: Lethargy and clumsiness are followed by confusion, irritability, sometimes hallucinations, and eventually coma.

claims.text: Diuresis plus fluid leaking into the tissues causes hypovolemia
claims.quote: Diuresis plus fluid leakage into the interstitial tissues causes hypovolemia.

claims.text: Treatment Diagnose with a core (not oral) temperature
claims.quote: Diagnosis is by measuring core, not oral, temperature

claims.text: Mild (32 to 35 °C): passive rewarming with heated blankets and warm fluids to drink is usually adequate
claims.quote: For mild hypothermia (32 to 35°C), passive rewarming with heated blankets and warm fluids to drink are usually adequate treatment.

claims.text: Moderate or severe (below about 32 °C): active rewarming, typically with forced-air warming, heated humidified oxygen and warm IV fluid, and sometimes heated lavage or extracorporeal methods
claims.quote: For moderate or severe hypothermia (below approximately 32° C), active rewarming should be performed, typically using forced-air hot air enclosures; heated, humidified oxygen; warm IV fluid; and sometimes heated lavage or extracorporeal methods (eg, cardiopulmonary bypass, hemodialysis).

claims.text: At lower temperatures patients are hypovolemic and need fluid resuscitation
claims.quote: At lower temperatures, patients are hypovolemic and require fluid resuscitation.

claims.text: Handle gently and keep horizontal during transport
claims.quote: During transport or evacuation, the patient should avoid physical effort, be handled gently, and remain horizontal.

claims.text: CPR with caution in hypothermic cardiac arrest; treat at a center capable of extracorporeal life support; ACLS drugs are usually not given until about 30 °C
claims.quote: CPR should be performed with caution in hypothermic cardiac arrest. Patients experiencing or at risk for hypothermic cardiac arrest should be treated at a center capable of extracorporeal life support and rewarming. Advanced cardiac life-support medications are usually not given until temperature reaches approximately 30° C.
